name: OODS Forge — Claude Desktop (stdio)
summary: Connect Claude Desktop to the OODS Forge runtime bundle through the stdio adapter.

env.MCP_EXTRA_TOOLS: comma-separated on-demand tools to add to the default surface, for example a11y.scan,diag.snapshot
env.OODS_NODE_PATH: absolute path of the Node binary the adapter should start the server with; default: the Node running the adapter
env.OODS_MCP_APPS_UI: 1 offers the design preview app to a client that did not negotiate the MCP Apps extension; default: unset, only clients that negotiated it

notes: Replace /path/to/forge-runtime with the directory you extracted forge-runtime.tar.gz into; the path must be absolute.
Node 20.11.1 or newer must be on the PATH as node, or set OODS_NODE_PATH.
The adapter starts the bundled native server itself; nothing else needs to be built, installed or running.
Default surface: 19 tools. MCP_TOOLSET=all advertises all 24.
Restart Claude Desktop after saving the file; the tools appear under the forge server.

Turn on Developer Mode to see design.preview as the running app inside the conversation: Claude Desktop renders apps from a local server only with Developer Mode on; otherwise the result is text with links to the preview in the browser, served by the adapter on 127.0.0.1.

Register forge directly, beside any other entry such as an MCP hub, not behind it: the preview app reaches the conversation only when the client talks to the adapter itself or a hub passes the MCP Apps extension, the tool's _meta.ui and resources/read through.
After replacing the runtime with a newer release, choose Reload MCP Configuration: Claude Desktop keeps the tool list and the preview app it fetched until then.
